# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

**Short answer: only partly.** A researcher can build a rough proxy analysis from public data, but cannot directly determine whether rural communities have less access to disability services than urban ones.

## Question
Can SSA public datasets be used to determine whether rural communities have less access to disability services than urban communities?

## Intent
- **Primary intent:** Determine whether rural communities have less access to SSA disability services than urban communities using available public datasets
- **Category:** Accessibility
- **Scope:** County level
- **Required data:** Field office locations, disability population distribution, county-level beneficiary counts, travel distance to nearest office, appointment wait times by geography

## Answer Coverage
**Partial**

## Available Data

| # | Data | Link | Source record |
|---|------|------|---------------|
| 1 | SSA Disability Claim Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-fywl.htm | Data.gov US-GOV-SSA-308 (metadata modified 2022-07-07; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 2 | Field Office Claims Pending | https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.html | US-GOV-SSA-435 (modified 2023-03-21; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description |
| 3 | 2016 Field Office Employee Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Field%20Office%20Employee%20Counts.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1918 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 4 | Field Office Contact Information | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-RS-Address-Open-Close-Time-App-Devs.html | US-GOV-SSA-1733 (modified 2026-03-09; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 5 | Field Office Telephone Service – Monthly National Answer Rate and Busy Rate | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-Answer-Busy-Rate.html | US-GOV-SSA-1414 (modified 2026-03-26; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 6 | 2016 Field Office Visitor Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY2016%20Field%20Office%20Visitor%20Counts.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1917 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 7 | Field Office Visitors (Average Daily) – FY 2006 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/field-office-visitors-average-daily.html | US-GOV-SSA-434 (modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 8 | Hearing Office Workload Data – Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/02_HO_Workload_Data.html | US-GOV-SSA-303 (modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 9 | OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County (series) | https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/statcomps/oasdi_sc/index.html | US-GOV-SSA-3378 (modified 2025-08-22; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 10 | SSI Recipients by State and County (series) | https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/statcomps/ssi_sc/index.html | US-GOV-SSA-3414 (modified 2025-08-15; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description |
| 11 | 2016 Title 2 Claim Receipts by Field Office | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Title%202%20Claim%20Receipts%20by%20Field%20Office.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1919 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |

## Missing Information
- Travel distance to nearest SSA field office
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times). Only indirect, one-time or discontinued data exist.

## Gap Analysis

**Not published** (no SSA dataset on Data.gov provides it):
- **Travel distance to nearest SSA field office (critical).** Checked: a Data.gov search of SSA datasets with downloads ('distance', 'travel', 'drive time') on 2026-11-22 found no dataset reporting distance or travel time to field offices.

**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):
- Geographic distribution of disability service access (critical)
- Field office operational metrics: staffing, volume, wait times (critical)

*(critical = the question cannot be answered without this information.)*

**Impact:** The question can only be partly answered. The information it depends on most, travel distance to the nearest field office, is not published. The geographic distribution of access is at least partly available, so part of an answer is possible.

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Geographic distribution of disability service access | Partial | Office locations (US-GOV-SSA-1733) can be joined to county beneficiary counts (US-GOV-SSA-3378, -3414). There are no service areas, travel times or per-office demand to measure access directly. |
| SSA field office locations and coverage | Full | Locations, phone numbers and hours of every field office are published and updated quarterly (US-GOV-SSA-1733). |
| Travel distance to nearest SSA field office | None | No SSA dataset on Data.gov reports travel distance or time. |
| Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) | Proxy | Per-office staffing, visitor and Title II disability claim receipt counts exist for FY2016 only (US-GOV-SSA-1917, -1918, -1919). The current series (daily visitors, claims pending, phone answer and busy rates) are national totals with no per-office figures. |

*Full: measured directly at the needed detail. Partial: measured but missing a level, breakdown or period. Proxy: only indirect, one-time or discontinued data. None: no SSA dataset found.*

## Transparency Recommendations

**Geographic detail**
1. Publish travel distance to nearest SSA field office by ZIP code or county. This closes the travel-distance gap. It is the most direct proxy for access burden, and without it rural and urban barriers to in-person service can't be quantified.
2. Publish county-level disability beneficiary counts alongside field office locations. This closes the geographic-distribution gap. It would show where SSA serves high-need populations well and where access lags need.

**Operational metrics**
3. Publish monthly visit volumes and appointment counts for each field office. Per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016, so offices can't be ranked by current demand.
4. Publish staffing FTE counts by field office every year. Per-office counts were released once, for FY2016. An annual series would show where caseload-per-staff ratios indicate strain.
5. Publish office service-capacity metrics (capacity utilisation, peak demand periods). These would support decisions on resource reallocation and new office openings.

**Access data**
6. Publish average appointment wait times by field office. Wait times are the most direct indicator of accessibility and demand pressure.
7. Publish average appointment wait times by rural vs. urban office classification. This would directly answer whether rural communities face longer delays.

## Potential Impact
Publishing these elements would let researchers and policymakers directly evaluate rural–urban gaps. They would support analysis of:
- Geographic disparities in service accessibility
- Travel burden to SSA field offices
- Appointment wait times by region
- Alignment of staffing with community demand
- Potential disability-service deserts and underserved areas

---
*Assessment basis: official dataset metadata (SSA's Data.gov records), recorded Data.gov searches for each gap, and curated analyst notes. Dataset contents were not downloaded or inspected.*

# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

**Short answer:** SSA's public data can't tell you which field offices have the longest decision wait times. Coverage is rated **Limited**.

## Question
Which field offices have the longest decision wait times?

## Intent
- **Primary intent:** Rank SSA offices by how long disability decisions take.
- **Category:** Performance
- **Scope:** Field office level
- **Required data:** Decision times by the office that decides the claim, pending claims by office, and a mapping of field offices to the offices that decide their claims.

**Note on the question:** Field offices take disability applications and check non-medical eligibility. They do not make the medical decision. Each state's Disability Determination Services (DDS) makes initial and reconsideration decisions. Hearing offices decide appeals. So decision times belong to those offices, not to field offices.

## Answer Coverage
**Limited**

## Available Data

| # | Data | Web Link | Source Record |
|---|------|----------|---------------|
| 1 | Field Office Claims Pending | https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.html | Data.gov US-GOV-SSA-435 (metadata modified 2023-03-21; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description. |
| 2 | 2016 Field Office Employee Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Field%20Office%20Employee%20Counts.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1918 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 3 | Field Office Contact Information | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-RS-Address-Open-Close-Time-App-Devs.html | US-GOV-SSA-1733 (modified 2026-03-09; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 4 | Field Office Telephone Service - Monthly National Answer Rate and Busy Rate | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-Answer-Busy-Rate.html | US-GOV-SSA-1414 (modified 2026-03-26; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 5 | 2016 Field Office Visitor Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY2016%20Field%20Office%20Visitor%20Counts.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1917 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 6 | Field Office Visitors (Average Daily) - FY 2006 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/field-office-visitors-average-daily.html | US-GOV-SSA-434 (modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 7 | Hearing Office Workload Data - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/02_HO_Workload_Data.html | US-GOV-SSA-303 (modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 8 | Average Wait Time Until Hearing Held Report - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/01_NetStat_Report.html | US-GOV-SSA-304 (modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 9 | Combined Title II Disability and Title XVI Blind and Disabled Average Processing Time - FY 2016 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/Combined-Disability-Processing-Time.html | US-GOV-SSA-1409 (modified 2026-03-31; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 10 | Disability Reconsideration Average Processing Time (Excludes technical denials) - FY2014 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/disability_reconsideration_average_processing_time.html | US-GOV-SSA-1768 (modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 11 | SSA State Agency Workload Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-mowl.htm | US-GOV-SSA-307 (modified 2023-08-08; synced 2026-11-22) |
| 12 | 2016 Title 2 Claim Receipts by Field Office | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Title%202%20Claim%20Receipts%20by%20Field%20Office.xlsx | US-GOV-SSA-1919 (modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22) |

## Missing Information
- Disability decision times by field office or DDS (only indirect, one-time or discontinued data)
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (only indirect, one-time or discontinued data)

## Gap Analysis

**Only partly available:**
- Disability decision times by field office or DDS (critical)
- Disability claim processing times
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (critical)

"Critical" means the question cannot be answered without this information.

**Impact:** The question can only be partly answered from public data. The information it depends on most is available only indirectly (one-time, historical or discontinued data).

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Disability decision times by field office or DDS | Proxy | No dataset reports decision times per field office or per DDS. Initial-claim times are national averages (US-GOV-SSA-1409). State agency data has pending counts by state but no times (US-GOV-SSA-307). Field office claims pending is one national count per year, all claim types combined, ending FY2022 (US-GOV-SSA-435). Per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303), which are not mapped to field offices. |
| Disability claim processing times | Partial | Average processing times are published for initial claims (-1409), reconsiderations (-1768) and hearings (-303, -304), but only as averages. No state breakdown is described for initial claims. |
| SSA field office locations and coverage | Full | Locations, phone numbers and hours of every field office are published and updated quarterly (US-GOV-SSA-1733). |
| Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) | Proxy | Per-office staffing, visitor and Title II disability claim receipt counts exist for FY2016 only (US-GOV-SSA-1917, -1918, -1919). The current series are national totals with no per-office figures: daily visitors (-434), claims pending (-435), and phone answer and busy rates (-1414). |

**Why Limited:** The two things this question needs most are only available indirectly (rated Proxy). Because of that, the rating can't go higher than Limited. The better-covered items can't make up for them.

## Transparency Recommendations

**Geographic Detail**
1. **Publish average time to an initial decision for claims taken at each field office.** This closes the gap on disability decision times by field office or DDS. Initial-claim time is published only as a national average (-1409), and per-office times exist only for hearing offices (-303).
2. **Publish state-level initial claim processing times.** This closes the gap on disability claim processing times. The -1409 record describes no state breakdown, and State Agency Workload Data (-307) has state counts without times.

**Operational Metrics**
3. **Publish monthly visit volumes and appointment counts for each field office.** Per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (-1917).
4. **Publish pending claims for each field office, not only the national total.** Field Office Claims Pending (-435) reports one national count per fiscal year, FY2006–2022, for all claim types combined.
5. **Publish staffing FTE counts by field office every year.** Per-office employee counts were released once, for FY2016 (-1918).
6. **Publish office service-capacity metrics (capacity utilisation, peak demand periods).** These would support decisions about resource reallocation and new office openings.

**Access Data**
7. **Publish average appointment wait times by field office.** These are the most direct indicator of service accessibility and demand pressure at the office level.
8. **Publish average appointment wait times by rural vs. urban office classification.** This would show whether rural communities face longer delays.

## Potential Impact
Publishing the missing data would substantially improve the public's ability to evaluate SSA program equity, efficiency and access.

---

cases.question: If SSA wanted to maximize public understanding of disability service accessibility, what additional datasets or metrics should be published first?

run.answer:
## Recommended publication order

These are the tool's ranked recommendations for improving public understanding of disability service accessibility.

### High priority

1. **Travel distance to the nearest SSA field office, by ZIP code or county.**
   - **Why it ranks high:** this information is not published at all (rated "None").
   - **Why it matters:** distance is the most direct proxy for access burden. Without it, no one can quantify whether rural communities face greater barriers than urban ones.
   - **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-locator`.

2. **Monthly visit volumes and appointment counts for each field office.**
   - **Why it ranks high:** it is only available indirectly (rated "Proxy").
   - **Current state:** SSA publishes a national average of daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434). Per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1917).
   - **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-visitors` and `ssa-field-office-visitor-counts-2016`.

3. **Monthly walk-in and appointment visit volumes by field office.**
   - **Why it ranks high:** it is a Proxy-rated gap.
   - **Why it matters:** it is the baseline demand measure for spotting access pressure points.
   - **Overlap:** this is close to item 2. The two could be published as a single release.

4. **Annual FTE staffing levels for field offices and hearing offices.**
   - **Why it ranks high:** it is a Proxy-rated gap.
   - **Current state:** field office staffing was released once, for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1918). The catalog has no hearing office staffing data.
   - **Why it matters:** it lets analysts normalize pending cases against staff capacity.
   - **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-locator` and `ssa-hearing-office-workload`.

### Medium priority (follow-ups)

5. **Annual field office FTE counts as a recurring series.** Combined with visit volumes, it would show caseload-per-staff strain. The FY2016 release is the only one so far.
6. **Percentage of visitors served within 30 and 60 minutes.** This turns volume data into a comparable service-time benchmark across offices.
7. **Adjudicator-to-caseload ratios alongside pending case counts.** This gives context to raw backlog numbers. It builds on `ssa-hearing-office-workload` and `ssa-hearing-wait-time`.
8. **Average appointment wait times by field office.** The only published appointment measure is a national series discontinued in 2015 (US-GOV-SSA-431).

### Summary

- **Four high-priority items:** distance, visit volumes, appointment and walk-in counts, and staffing.
- **Distance:** the tool rates it the most critical gap because nothing is published.
- **Visit volumes and staffing:** only the 2016 per-office data exists for these.
- **Wait times and service-time benchmarks:** these are medium priority follow-ups.

cases.question: What can the Field Office Claims Pending dataset tell me, and what can't it?

run.answer:
## Field Office Claims Pending (`ssa-field-office-claims-pending`)

**What it is:** A yearly national count of all claims pending in SSA field offices. These are claims in process and not yet adjudicated. It is published on the SSA Open Data Portal and updated annually. The last metadata update was 2023-03-21.

**What it can tell you**
- The national trend in field office claim backlogs by fiscal year.
- The count covers all claim types:
  - Retirement and Survivor Insurance (RSI)
  - RSI Dependent
  - Disability Insurance (DI)
  - DI Dependent
  - SSI Aged
  - SSI Blind/Disabled
- The key fields are `fiscal_year` and `claims_pending`, which is the count at year end.
- Download links are the [page](https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.html) and the [CSV](https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.csv).

**What it can't tell you**
- **Geography:** It gives a national total only. There are no per-office or per-state counts.
- **Disability specifically:** All claim types are combined, so disability claims are not broken out.
- **Timing:** It has pending counts only. It has no processing or wait times.
- **Recency:** It ends at FY2022. The catalog gives the temporal coverage as 2005–2022 per the Data.gov record. The dataset description says FY2006–2022, so the start year is inconsistent between the two.
- **Granularity:** It is annual, so there is no monthly or within-year view.

**Caveats**
- The field list comes from the official metadata description. It has not been checked column by column against the data dictionary (`fields_verified: false`).
- The update frequency is inferred from the record's description.

**Related datasets the catalog returned**
- `ssa-state-agency-workload-data`: monthly pending counts by state. These cover cases at the state agency (DDS) for disability determination, not field offices.
- `ssa-initial-disability-processing-time`: processing time for initial disability claims.
- `ssa-title2-claim-receipts-by-field-office-2016`: Title 2 disability claim receipts by field office, FY2016 only.

I can run a coverage evaluation on a specific question, such as per-office backlogs, or recommend what SSA should publish to close these gaps.

# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

## Question
Does SSA publish disability decision wait times for every field office?

## Intent
**Primary intent**: Rank SSA offices by how long disability decisions take
**Category**: Performance
**Scope**: Field office level
**Required data**: Decision times by the office that decides the claim, pending claims by office, and a mapping of field offices to the offices that decide their claims

**Note on the question**: Field offices take disability applications and check non-medical eligibility, but they don't make the medical decision. Each state's Disability Determination Services (DDS) makes initial and reconsideration decisions. Hearing offices decide appeals. Decision times therefore belong to those offices.

## Answer Coverage
**Limited**

## Available Data

## Missing Information
- Disability decision times by field office or DDS. Only indirect, one-time or discontinued data exists.

## Gap Analysis
**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):
- Disability decision times by field office or DDS (critical)
- Disability claim processing times

(critical): the question cannot be answered without this information.

**Impact**: The question can only be partly answered from public data. The information it depends on most is available only indirectly: disability decision times by field office or DDS.

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Disability decision times by field office or DDS | Proxy | No dataset reports decision times per field office or per DDS. Initial-claim times are national averages (US-GOV-SSA-1409). State agency data has pending counts by state but no times (US-GOV-SSA-307). Field office claims pending is one national count per year, all claim types combined, ending FY2022 (US-GOV-SSA-435). Per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303), which are not mapped to field offices. |
| Disability claim processing times | Partial | Average processing times are published for initial claims (US-GOV-SSA-1409), reconsiderations (US-GOV-SSA-1768) and hearings (US-GOV-SSA-303, -304). They are averages only, with no state breakdown described for initial claims. |
| SSA field office locations and coverage | Full | Locations, phone numbers and hours of every field office are published and updated quarterly (US-GOV-SSA-1733). |

**Why Limited**: The most important item, disability decision times by field office or DDS, is rated Proxy. That caps the overall rating at Limited.

## Transparency Recommendations

**[Geographic Detail]**
1. **Publish average time to an initial decision for claims taken at each field office.** This closes the gap on decision times by field office or DDS. Initial-claim time is published only as a national average (US-GOV-SSA-1409). Per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303).
2. **Publish state-level initial claim processing times.** This closes the gap on claim processing times. US-GOV-SSA-1409 describes no state breakdown, and US-GOV-SSA-307 has state counts without times.

**[Operational Metrics]**
3. **Publish pending claims for each field office, not only the national total.** This closes the gap on decision times by field office or DDS. US-GOV-SSA-435 reports one national count per fiscal year, FY2006–2022, for all claim types combined.

**[Temporal Granularity]**
4. **Track end-to-end processing time across all decision levels.** This closes the gap on claim processing times. Initial, reconsideration and hearing times are published separately, as averages for different claim groups, so they can't be added into one claimant's wait.

## Potential Impact
Publishing the missing data elements would substantially improve the public's ability to evaluate SSA program equity, efficiency and access.
